name: GFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate)
seoDesc: GFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate): work out your result from the age and the serum creatinine. A free health calculator with the formula, units…
summary:
Supply the age, the serum creatinine and the serum cystatin C and the GFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate) calculator solves for the answer. It suits an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis.

The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the GFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate) calculator work?
sections.html:
The GFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate) calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationships described below and reports every result it can derive from them.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the sex and the ethnicity); then you type in the age, the serum creatinine and the serum cystatin C.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• Pick the option that matches your case — 3 options, such as serum creatinine, serum cystatin C and both serums. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 2 options, such as female and male. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 2 options, such as black and white / Hispanic / Asian / Other. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in years. The unit chip switches it to any of the 27 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in milligrams per deciliter. The unit chip switches it to any of the 3 supported units.
  • A number, expressed in mg/L.

3 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the GFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate) calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

CKD-EPI (2009)=(141 × (1000 ÷ 993 ^ -age) × ethnicity × sex × (the smaller of (1, -90 × serum creatinine ÷ (1000 × sex − 1081)), (41 ÷ 9) × sex − 44699 ÷ 9000) ÷ (the larger of (1, -90 × serum creatinine ÷ (1000 × sex − 1081)), 1209 ÷ 1000))
CKD-EPI Cystatin C (2012)=((133 ÷ 9) × (249 ^ age) × (250 ^ -age) × (43 − 34 × sex) ÷ ((the larger of (1, (5 ÷ 4) × serum cystatin C), 166 ÷ 125) × (the smaller of (1, (5 ÷ 4) × serum cystatin C), 499 ÷ 1000)))
MDRD=((175 ÷ 9) × (-172 × ethnicity × sex + 184 × ethnicity + 43 × sex − 46) ÷ ((serum creatinine ^ 577 ÷ 500) × (age ^ 203 ÷ 1000)))
CKD-EPI Creatinine-Cystatin (2012)=((199 ^ age) × (200 ^ -age − 2) × (-4679202 × ethnicity × sex + 7396158 × ethnicity − 4620705 × sex + 7303695) × (the smaller of (1, -90 × serum creatinine ÷ (1000 × sex − 1081)), 18637 ÷ 9000 − 41 ÷ 18 × sex) ÷ ((the larger of (1, (5 ÷ 4) × serum cystatin C), 711 ÷ 1000) × (the larger of (1, -90 × serum creatinine ÷ (1000 × sex − 1081)), 601 ÷ 1000) × (the smaller of (1, (5 ÷ 4) × serum cystatin C), 3 ÷ 8)))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Take Calculate E gfr based on set to Serum creatinine, Sex set to Female, Ethnicity set to Black and Age = 10 yrs. The calculator returns CKD-EPI (2009) = 7, MDRD = 44, CKD-EPI Creatinine-Cystatin (2012) = 5 and CKD-EPI Cystatin C (2012) = 4.

The point of the example is the scale, not the particular digits: swap in your own figures and the same relationship produces your answer.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: CKD-EPI (2009) = 7, MDRD = 44, CKD-EPI Creatinine-Cystatin (2012) = 5 and CKD-EPI Cystatin C (2012) = 4 should be roughly the size you expected from Calculate E gfr based on set to Serum creatinine and Sex set to Female.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Time, opening in years
  • Creatinine, opening in milligrams per deciliter

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The GFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate) calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the age, the serum creatinine and the serum cystatin C — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the GFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate) calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the age, the serum creatinine and the serum cystatin C, which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter age in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Age opens in years and the chip beside it offers 27 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (3 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports CKD-EPI (2009) = 7. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the GFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate) calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
